BA.name: Bankatlal
BA.identity_paragraph: Bankatlal Agarwal: an adult man of about 35, medium height, slightly full build, kind attentive face, small neat moustache, warm brown skin. He wears a cream-white turban wound in a round pagadi, a long sage-green cotton angarkha coat to below the knee, tied at the side, over a white dhoti, and a cream shoulder cloth (uparna) over his left shoulder. Barefoot. Nothing in his hands unless stated.

DK.name: Damodarpant
DK.identity_paragraph: Damodarpant Kulkarni: an adult man of about 35, lean and slightly taller than Bankatlal, narrow face, thin moustache, warm brown skin. He wears a terracotta-red Maharashtrian pagadi turban, a plain white long-sleeved cotton angarkha shirt to the knee, a white dhoti, and an off-white uparna over one shoulder. Barefoot.

GM.name: Gajanan Maharaj
GM.identity_paragraph: Shri Gajanan Maharaj: a young man in the prime of youth (looks about 25 to 30), strong and well built, muscular upper arms and neck, broad chest, radiant calm handsome face, eyes half-lowered with the gaze resting on the tip of his nose, short cropped dark hair, clean-shaven, warm medium-brown skin. He wears only one old, worn, torn sleeveless bandi (a short open-front vest) of faded grey-white cloth with frayed edges, and a minimal plain off-white loincloth; otherwise bare. Barefoot, no jewellery, no beads, no forehead mark. His only belongings: a dried bottle-gourd water vessel (natural tan, narrow neck) and a small hand-made unfired clay chilim (a straight conical clay pipe, matte raw grey-brown clay, never kiln-fired).

ROAD.name: Road before Devidas's house
ROAD.identity_paragraph: The road in front of Devidas's house in Shegaon: a dusty unpaved village road running across the picture; on the left a modest but solid village house with thick mud-plastered ochre walls, a terracotta clay-tile roof, a raised earthen plinth step (ota) and a heavy plain wooden door standing half open onto a dark interior; neighbouring low houses and neem trees further down the road. On the road in front of the door lie several used leaf plates (round plates of stitched dry leaves) with a few scattered grains of leftover white rice.

SHEGAON.name: Shegaon
SHEGAON.identity_paragraph: Shegaon in the 1870s: a small village on the flat open plain of Varhad, dark-brown soil, a cluster of low houses with mud-plastered walls in ochre and earth tones, some roofs of terracotta clay tiles and some thatched, a few neem and babul trees, dusty lanes, no temple spire, no large buildings, no people in view.
